extracted.intended_audience: readers of celebrity/news sites and general public interested in celebrity controversies
extracted.subtask_description: A short news report about a comedian's offensive social-media jokes and the resulting corporate response, focusing on brand risk and public apology. Useful for understanding real-world consequences when humor targets recent tragedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid joking about tragedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not make jokes about recent natural disasters or human tragedies (example: tweets about the earthquake and tsunami in Japan).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article reports that Aflac dismissed the comedian after he tweeted jokes about the earthquake and subsequent tsunami in Japan; the company said his comments "were lacking in humor and certainly do not represent the thoughts and feelings of anyone at Aflac." Consequence: loss of ad role as the duck's voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider audiences and key markets
rubrics_metrics.description: Performers and spokespeople must consider the sensitivities of markets where the brand operates (Japan was described as a key market for Aflac).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aflac has a different advertising voice in the Japanese market and emphasized its market significance; offending audiences in a key market can prompt corporate distancing and replacement of talent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public figures' social media reflect on employers
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements made publicly by a celebrity (e.g., tweets) are taken to reflect on affiliated companies and can trigger employment or contract consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gottfried's tweets led directly to Aflac's decision to dismiss him from their campaign despite his long tenure (voice of the duck since 2000), illustrating employer sensitivity to representatives' public conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue a prompt public apology when offense is caused
rubrics_metrics.description: When a public comment offends, the speaker should issue a clear apology acknowledging harm (example: Gottfried's statement: "I sincerely apologize to anyone who was offended by my attempt at humor regarding the tragedy in Japan.").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The apology is part of reputational management; while it may mitigate backlash, it does not guarantee restoration of roles or relationships with employers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporate response: distance brand and replace endorsers
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies will publicly distance themselves from offending remarks and take steps to replace or recast brand voices to protect corporate image.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aflac publicly stated the comedian's comments did not represent the company and announced a nationwide casting call for a new voice; they already used a different voice in the Japanese market, showing practical measures companies take after such incidents.
